description.narrative: Det övergripande målet för programmet "Visualizing the Energy State of Africa – addressing the energy vision of the African Union" är att stödja förverkligandet av Afrikanska unionens långsiktiga vision om att ge allmän tillgång till överkomliga, moderna och rena energitjänster. Stödet baseras på insikten om att välinformerat beslutsfattande, regionalt samarbete och starka institutioner är avgörande för att uppnå Afrikanska unionens energivision och vikten av att påskynda det som görs för att nå denna vision. Programmet stödjer AFREC, AU:s energikommission vars mandat är att främja samarbete på energiområdet mellan alla 55 afrikanska medlemsstater. Det inriktas på att stödja pågående arbete med att utveckla ett starkt, samordnat och harmoniserat energiinformationssystem och på att stödja verksamhet som kopplad till insamling och analys av data, erfarenhetsutbyte och och kapacitetsuppbyggnad. Målen för programmet är: 1) Ett starkt, samordnat och harmoniserat afrikanskt energiinformationssystem 2) Kapacitetsuppbyggnad av afrikanska institutioner och människor, och 3) Utveckla AFREC till en stark och relevant aktör för energisektorn i Afrika.

The overall objective of the programme titled "Visualizing the Energy State of Africa – addressing the energy vision of the African Union" is to support the realisation of the African Union's long-term vision of bringing universal access to affordable, modern, and clean energy services. The support recognizes that well-informed decision-making, regional cooperation and strong institutions are key to the achievement of the African Union’s energy vision and the need to accelerate efforts serving this end. The programme will support AFREC, a specialised agency under AU’s Commission for Infrastructure and Energy with a mandate to advance cooperation in the area of energy among all its 55 African Member States. It will support AFREC’s ongoing work to develop a strong, coordinated and harmonized energy information system and support activities relating to collection and analysis of data, sharing of lessons learned and capacity-building. The outcome objectives for the programme are as follows:
1) A strong, coordinated and harmonised African Energy Information System 2) Capacity building of African institutions and people, and 3) Developing AFREC to a strong and relevant actor for the energy sector in Africa.

The long-term objective of the proposed program is to contribute to the African Union's long-term vision for energy: To support the Africa Agenda 2063, by bringing universal access to affordable, modern, and clean energy services. This will be done by strengthening the visibility, credibility, reputation, and relevance of AFREC to implement its broad mandate. It is intended that this operation will be the start of a long-term cooperation between Sida and AFREC.
The objective of the proposed intervention is to contribute to the development of Africa's energy sector by achieving:
i) a strong, coordinated and harmonized African energy information system,
ii) capacity building of African institutions and people; and
iii) developing AFREC into a strong and relevant actor for the energy sector in Africa.
Sida's assessment is that the proposed support to AFREC would strengthen AFREC's and member countries' ability to analyze the energy sector and make decisions based on sound information. The primary target group for the activities and outputs of the operation is the energy institutions of the Member States and, in the long term, the population of Africa.
The three separate but interlinked components build on a chain of activities, their expected results, and outcomes, which constitutes the theory of chain of the program. Each component has its specific goals and theory of change. The majority of activities will be conducted within Component 1 (65% of project implementation budget).
Component 1: Strong, coordinated, and harmonised African Energy Information System (AEIS) - Enhancing Capacity and Quality Data for the African Energy Sector
The aim of program component 1 is to implement the holistic improvement plan of the AEIS, which was developed in 2019, and to strengthen and speed up the work. The long-term objective of the component is to reach a strong, coordinated, and harmonised AEIS.
Component 2: Capacity building of African institutions and people
The main objective of component 2 is to identify skills gap in the field of the renewable energy sector, and design accordingly an online educational training package that will improve the capacity of policymakers, energy planners, regulators and experts from AU Member States, Regional Economic Communities, regional power pools, regional centers for renewable energy and energy efficiency, and other relevant stakeholders in the African energy sector.
Component 3: Developing AFREC to a strong and relevant actor in the energy sector in Africa Building the brand of AFREC
This component aims to strengthen the African leadership and ownership of the process towards successful energy sector development.
